sections.html:
Webster County sits in central Iowa, where Fort Dodge is both the seat of government and the biggest city. It borders Pocahontas and Humboldt to the north, Wright to the northeast, Hamilton to the east, Boone to the southeast, Greene to the southwest and Calhoun to the west.

In 2020 the census found 36,999 residents, and a 2025 estimate puts the number at 36,838. The county peaked at 48,391 people in 1970 and has lost population since.

The median owner-occupied home is worth $153,800 for 2020 to 2024, with 70.3 percent of homes occupied by owners. Mid-2025 housing units were estimated at 17,209. Rent runs a median $785 a month, and median household income is $68,975.

These are county medians. A Fort Dodge house, a farm dwelling near Gowrie and a small town house in Lehigh can differ widely in value.

sections.h2: Fort Dodge and the local economy
sections.html:
Fort Dodge began as an army post in 1850, was renamed for Henry Dodge, and was incorporated in 1869. A gypsum mill opened in 1872, and gypsum and limestone mining remain part of the economy alongside biofuels, livestock feed, can production, drywall, trucking and veterinary pharmaceuticals.

  • National Gypsum, Georgia Pacific, CertainTeed and United States Gypsum have plants in or near the city.
  • Elanco, which makes animal health products, has two of its three U.S. manufacturing plants in Fort Dodge.
  • Cargill announced a corn syrup refinery in 2022.
  • The city's lone hospital is UnityPoint, and Iowa Central Community College keeps its central campus here.

Meatpacking led local industry for most of the 20th century until the last two large plants shut in the 1980s. Industrial towns with a shrinking population tend to have older houses and modest prices.

Winters are cold and summers hot and humid. A year brings 35.09 inches of precipitation and 39.0 inches of snow on average, and extremes run from minus 35 degrees F to 110 degrees F. Roof, insulation and furnace condition carry weight here when a seller weighs repairs against selling as-is.

US 20 runs through the middle of the county and skirts Fort Dodge on the south, and US 169 passes to the west. Iowa 7 stops at the city's northwest edge, and Iowa 175 and Iowa 144 serve the southeast and south. Fort Dodge Regional Airport, just north of the city, has daily flights to St. Louis and Minneapolis-St. Paul, and DART runs six local bus routes on weekdays.

School districts include Fort Dodge, Webster City, Eagle Grove, Gilmore City-Bradgate, Humboldt, Manson Northwest Webster, Stratford and Southeast Valley, which formed in 2023 from a merger.

Find the treasurer, assessor, recorder and auditor together in the Webster County Courthouse at 701 Central Avenue, Fort Dodge, generally open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

  • Treasurer: 515-576-4611. Online payment is available at iowatreasurers.org.
  • Assessor: 515-576-4721, assessor@webstercountyia.gov. Look up property records on the county's Beacon site.
  • Recorder: 515-576-2401. The recording cutoff for real estate is 3:00 p.m. The office also collects transfer tax for the Iowa Department of Revenue.
  • Auditor: 515-573-7175. This office prepares and certifies tax levies and keeps real estate transfer records.

Real property is revalued in odd-numbered years, effective January 1, and market value means what the property would likely sell for on that date. Notices arrive in March.

Informal meetings with the county's appraisal contractor begin April 2, and appointments are requested through the assessor at 515-576-4721. Written Board of Review protests are accepted April 2 through April 30. Three or five members sit on the Board, which can raise or lower a value.

If you disagree with the decision, appeal to the Property Assessment Appeal Board or the district court within 20 days after the Board adjourns or by May 31, whichever comes later.

The county also reappraised agricultural dwellings and rural residential property from 2024 to 2026. Those new values start January 1, 2026 and apply to taxes payable in fiscal 2027 and 2028.

sections.h2: Levy rates and the EMS tax
sections.html:
For fiscal 2025 to 2026 the county levy was $7.12 per $1,000 of taxable value for urban property, including Fort Dodge, and $10.78 for rural property. The county's tax asking was $19,578,775, up less than 1 percent.

The levy includes a new EMS tax of 75 cents per $1,000, which voters approved on March 4, 2025 by an 83 percent margin. It is expected to raise about $1.6 million a year.

In March 2026 the county said residential rates fell 2.37 percent for urban property and 1.76 percent for rural, while commercial rates rose 4.97 percent and 5.62 percent. Some owners still saw higher bills because assessments went up.

sections.h2: Due dates, tax sale and transfer tax
sections.html:
Two installments are due, September 1 and March 1, and interest of 1.5 percent a month begins October 1 and April 1. A sale normally prorates taxes, giving the buyer credit for the seller's share.

Delinquent parcels may be sold at tax sale. Getting one back costs the sale amount plus 2 percent a month and $20 each in certificate and redemption fees, and if the redemption period lapses a tax sale deed can follow.

Under Iowa Code 428A.3 the seller pays the state transfer tax, 80 cents for each $500 past the first $500.

Ordinance 2204 of the municipal code requires Fort Dodge rentals to be registered and inspected. An updated rental ordinance with a four-star rating system took effect October 1, 2022.

A unit rented without a valid certificate of rental housing compliance may be ordered vacated, and the owner may be cited. The city's Neighborhood Wellness Coordinator is at City Hall, 819 1st Avenue South, 515-576-4551 extension 1252. A landlord leaving a rental that needs work can sell it without repairs.

sections.h2: Selling a Webster County house as-is
sections.html: Webster County houses are bought in any condition here, rentals needing work and houses with unpaid taxes included. Email or call with the address and latest tax statement and a written offer follows. The title company clears taxes and liens from the proceeds at closing and hands you the remainder. Before you call, collect the deed, any mortgage payoff figure, and the rental compliance certificate if the house is a rental, since the title search goes faster with them. You choose the closing date, and no lender appraisal is involved.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Webster County, Iowa?
faqs.a: Fort Dodge, the largest city, with 24,871 residents in 2020. County offices are at the courthouse, 701 Central Avenue.

faqs.q: When can I protest a Webster County assessment?
faqs.a: The Board of Review takes written protests April 2 through April 30. For an informal look first, call the assessor at 515-576-4721.

faqs.q: How much is the new Webster County EMS tax?
faqs.a: 75 cents per $1,000 of taxable value. Voters approved it on March 4, 2025, and it is expected to raise about $1.6 million a year.

faqs.q: Does Webster County have a tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax can be sold, and the owner redeems with the amount sold, 2 percent per month and fees. The treasurer at 515-576-4611 can quote a payoff.

faqs.q: Who pays Iowa transfer tax in Webster County?
faqs.a: The seller, at 80 cents per $500 past the first $500. The recorder collects it before the deed is recorded.
